subject: Seaforth Azure private listing: term & rev-share exception request
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Louis Sanders <louis.sanders@seaforthenergy.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Private listing for Seaforth — Azure private offer terms

Louis —

Great speaking yesterday. Per our call, Seaforth is a strong fit for our Azure private listing and we can fast-track the onboarding. I've attached the latest SOW and a first-pass private offer draft for marketplace listing. A few items to flag that need special handling on your side and ours:

- Seaforth has requested Net-60 payment terms (standard is Net-30 for marketplace billings).
- Procurement would like a 12% rev-share instead of the standard 15% for the first 12 months.
- You requested consolidated monthly billing routed via your Azure billing account.

To progress, I need to confirm whether we can escalate for a one-time deviation on rev-share and payment terms with Finance and Deal Desk. Can you confirm the procurement contact I should loop into the DocuSign and whether there is a minimum committed spend you can commit to for the first 12 months?

Attaching: Seaforth_SOW_v2.pdf; Seaforth_Azure_Private_Offer_Draft.docx

Next steps: I will request internal approval today and follow up with a timeline for listing once terms are agreed.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Thanks, Sean.

Claire (procurement) is copied. For clarity: Seaforth is asking for Net-60 because our corporate billing cycles are setup that way; it is non-negotiable without internal approvals. We are prepared to sign a 12-month minimum commitment of $180k ARR for the listing, but need rev-share at 12% for the first year to hit our pricing targets.

We can accept the marketplace billing flow via our Azure subscription. If you can get internal sign-off on Net-60 and 12% rev-share, we can move to a DocuSign this week.

-Louis

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:45:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Seaforth private listing — need exec exception for Net-60 + rev-share

Team — forwarding Seaforth request. Summary: external asks Net-60 and 12% rev-share for 12 months in exchange for $180k ARR commitment.

Can Deal Desk and Finance evaluate the top-line impact and flag any compliance/legal issues for marketplace listings? We need an executive exception to proceed (this will alter standard marketplace cashflow and revenue recognition).

Notes:
- Sales willing to take a one-time commission adjustment if that helps.
- Legal: confirm wording for the private offer so we don't violate marketplace terms re: billing cycles.

Attaching revenue model from Sean. Karthik, please advise on the smallest set of guardrails we need if this is approved (minimum commit, clawbacks, pilot discount window).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of GTM Partnerships — Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Seaforth private listing — need exec exception for Net-60 + rev-share

Vanessa / Sean —

Thanks. Quick assessment:
- Rev-share impact: moving from 15% to 12% reduces Redwood's take by ~20% on marketplace margin for the first 12 months. With the $180k ARR commitment, expected reduction is roughly $5.4k in FY1 margin (see attached model).
- Net-60: cash flow hit is material for marketplace settlements; we typically avoid Net-60 for marketplace flows because of billing reconciliation lag with vendor marketplaces (AWS).

Alternatives that would be easier to approve without exec signoff: 45-day payment term, or keep Net-30 with a 30-day receivable extension arranged between Redwood and Seaforth off-market (requires legal + finance escrow). Could also approve 12% rev-share for a 6-month pilot instead of 12 months.

If you want a formal exception, we'll need an exec approval email that:
1) Authorizes Net-60 for the Seaforth Azure private listing,
2) Approves 12% rev-share for 12 months,
3) Signs off on a minimum $180k committed spend and a clawback if commitment not met.

Attached: seaforth_revenue_model.xlsx (impact calc)

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Deal Desk Manager — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Seaforth private listing — term exception decision

Team —

I reviewed the ask and the impact workbook. Approve with conditions. Executive exception granted under the following terms:

1) Net-60 billing is approved for Seaforth only if Redwood receives cleared payment terms evidence via Azure invoice routing and a signed acknowledgement from Seaforth procurement that ties the commitment to the Azure account. Finance must confirm a deferred revenue tracking entry before listing.

2) Rev-share reduced to 12% is approved for the first 12 months, conditioned on a $180k minimum committed spend executed in DocuSign. If the commitment is not met within 12 months, the rev-share will revert to 15% and a pro-rated clawback will apply.

3) Legal to include explicit clawback language, billing routing instructions, and a 30-day grace for reconciliation disputes.

Karthik/Vanessa: please document the exception in the Deal Desk exceptions log and notify AWS Marketplace Ops with the private offer doc. Sean — proceed to get DocuSign executed and confirm hubspot stage to Closed Won only after finance confirms deferred revenue setup.

Markus Klein
Chief Revenue Officer — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
